summary: Ground cabin on McPherson Peak, built 1934 and staffed 1935-39; removal date disputed, and the summit held Air Force communication arrays in 2011.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 ground cabin, not on a tower
facts.status_note: Structure removed or burned after 1984 (sources disagree on which); mounting piers and a concrete cistern remain per the register; a 2011 visit found Air Force communication arrays on the summit.
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Los Padres National Forest

visit.trail_note: A 3.35-mile McPherson Trail is listed by a trail guide; no source says whether the summit is open to visitors.

events.note: Ground cabin, California Region 5 Plan BC-301; no tower
Two CCC men named to fire lookouts; Bill Hoey put in charge at McPherson with a radio
July 1935 fire fanned by a 35-mile wind came within 400 yards of the station
Conrad Munson assigned to the lookout
Munson relieved in December 1939 as the last of the district's protection force for the season
Bids announced for an eight-mile fire protection road to the lookout
Photo caption: in poor condition and not in service, November 1984
Single source (trail guide) says the facility burned April 7, 1987; FFLOS and Carey say removed
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register December 20, 2019

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says removed sometime after 1984; Carey says removed in the late 1980s; a trail guide says the facility burned April 7, 1987. A November 1984 photo caption already shows it out of service. The sources are not reconciled, so the story reports each account.

sources.title: Mcpherson Trail - Los Padres National Forest

notes_for_editor: Access is unknown: no source says whether the summit is open to visitors. Removal has three accounts (after 1984 per FFLOS; late 1980s per Carey; burned April 7, 1987 per one trail guide), and the burned date rests on a single source whose 'facility' is ambiguous (communication site or lookout). No corrections to the brief: slug, ground-cabin kind, 1934 build and 2019 registration all check out. Staffing dates come from 1935-39 newspaper excerpts, not an official roster. No photos added: the FFLOS and peakbagging pages carry captions only, and no image URLs were retrieved.
